plain.text: Israel set out with all he had. At Beersheba he offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac. God spoke to him in a vision at night: "Jacob, Jacob!" "Here I am." "I am God, the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there. I will go down with you to Egypt, and I will surely bring you back again. And Joseph's own hand will close your eyes." So Jacob and all his descendants went to Egypt in the carts Pharaoh had sent.

These are the names of the Israelites who went to Egypt: Jacob and his descendants, listed by mothers: the children and grandchildren of Leah, of her servant Zilpah, of Rachel (including Joseph's sons, born in Egypt, and Benjamin's), and of Rachel's servant Bilhah. Altogether, the members of Jacob's family who went to Egypt were seventy.

Jacob sent Judah ahead to Joseph to get directions to Goshen. Joseph prepared his chariot and went to meet his father. As soon as Joseph appeared before him, he threw his arms around his father and wept for a long time. Israel said, "Now I am ready to die, since I have seen for myself that you are still alive." Joseph told his brothers how to speak to Pharaoh: they should say they had always been shepherds, so they could live in Goshen, because Egyptians looked down on shepherds.

summary.bigIdea: God tells Jacob not to be afraid to go to Egypt, and Jacob is reunited with Joseph at last.
points: God promises, "I will go down with you to Egypt, and I will surely bring you back."
Seventy members of Jacob's family move to Egypt.
Joseph and his father embrace and weep for a long time.
summary.reflection: God told Jacob, "Do not be afraid... I will go down with you." Where do you need to hear that God goes with you?
